answer: Because marriage vows are legally binding until the couple breaks them, you can’t simply move out or stop financially supporting him. If you leave or refuse to keep house or teach the kids, you may be required to pay him alimony for the rest of your life. You also have to sign property transfers because the union owns everything jointly. The time to end the marriage is usually right before the remarriage is final, or you run the risk of facing penalties. So figure out whether you can stay in love or plan to go back—exploring other options before that final stage is often best avoided.
